To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Merkel cell-neurites are patterned by Bmp4-exposing dermal cells, epidermal Nogging, and Keratin-17 expressing keratinocytes during development.

touch domes are a distinct skin structure that emerge at E16.5 and contain three cell types, Merkel cells, Bmp4-exposing cells, and Keratin 17-expressing epidermal keratinocytes that are required for Merkel-cell innervation.
touch domes are composed of a cluster of keratinocytes, Merkel cells, and dermal cells and that Merkel cells are not the only cells that are important for Merkel-cell innervation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the mechanosensory system, which is the primary sensory system that provides us with information about the external world.
understanding the cellular mechanisms that underlie the development of touch sensation in mammals.
the development and function of the skin, and in particular, how the skin senses touch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cellular basis of mechanoreceptive Merkel cell-neuronal complexes is established during embryogenesis and is dependent upon the presence of a unique population of Bmp-expressing cells, the expression of Noggin in the epidermis, and the presence of Keratin-17 expressing epidermal cells.
Merkel cell development is dependent on the expression of Bmp4 by dermal cells.
Merkel-cell afferent neurons innervate touch domes during skin development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Merkel cells are the mechanosensory receptors in the touch domes, and the Bmp4-expressed dermal cells, Keratin-16/17-expressed keratinocytes, and Merkel cells are required for proper innervation of the touch domes by Merkel cell-neurites during development.
Merkel cell afferents are targeted to touch domes by Bmp4-expressed dermal cells, but only one of the two neuronal populations persists.

Merkel cell afferents are patterned by a complex interplay of keratinocytes, Merkel cells and dermal cells during development, and that the cellular basis of Merkel cell innervation is distinct from that of hair follicle innervation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Merkel-cell afferent targeting is not simply a function of Merkel cells but also involves other cell types, such as keratinocytes and Bmp4-ex-pressing dermal progenitors, and requires distinct signaling pathways.
touch domes are not just a collection of Merkel cells, but rather a specialized epidermal-dermal unit that is necessary for the proper development of touch domes.
the cellular basis of Merkel-cell innervation is much more complex than originally thought.
